reason: A 42-person, $14M-seed "AI-native" fund-admin platform whose live Fund Controller posting asks the hire to "translate accounting standards and edge cases into scalable systems" while today's board carries eight-plus fund-accounting/ops hires against a single Ruby on Rails engineer — cost-to-deliver still scaling one-for-one with accounts, which is exactly the services-to-product transition and EDP Daniel sells.

company.name: Decile Group

people_spec: Chief Executive Officer (Adeo Ressi) — owns the gross-margin/cost-to-serve consequence and the services-to-product thesis; primary buyer at 42 people

Head of Product and Technology (Travis Giggy) — the closest thing to an engineering leader; there is no CTO or VP of Engineering at this company, so this title owns the platform roadmap and the one-engineer-per-eight-ops-hires ratio
Head of Operations — currently held and simultaneously re-posted as 'Head of Operations (Remote)'; owns the human delivery layer whose headcount is the problem
VP of Finance (Remote) / Acting CFO — open and interim respectively; owns the cost-to-deliver number itself
Note: no CTO, VP Engineering, or Head of Platform exists or is being hired — do not look for one
talk_track: I work on one transition: businesses that proved demand with a high-touch, human-delivered offer and now need that work to live in systems instead of in people. I ran platform engineering at PayPal and Ripple, and at Tricentis I put AI agents into production for incident detection and root-cause analysis. Your Fund Controller posting says the role "partners with Product and Engineering teams to help translate accounting standards and edge cases into scalable systems," and the Sales, Fund Solutions posting sells "AI handles the heavy lifting. Ultra-senior staff on every account." Set those against the rest of your Lever board today — Fund Accountant, Senior Fund Accountant, Fund Controller, Legal Operations Associate, Deals Associate, Head of Operations — next to one Ruby on Rails engineer. The non-obvious read is that the agentic layer is real at the front end, but the accounting judgment that sets cost-to-serve is still being hired one person at a time, so each new fund adds cost about as fast as it adds revenue. That ratio, not the pipeline, is what decides whether gross margin expands as you scale past 150 partner firms. Where does that edge-case judgment live today — product, or people? — Daniel Kirichanski, Prime Path Global
